verdict.reasoning: I rendered page 897 (printed p.873) at 300 dpi. Figure D.11 shows Entrance -> box 'Set identifier-2 equal to current FROM value' -> rounded node 'Condition-1'. From Condition-1, 'True' goes right to 'Exit' and 'False' goes down to box 'Execute specified set of statements', then to box 'Augment identifier-2 with current BY value'. A line leaves the left side of the Augment box, runs up the left margin and enters Condition-1 with an arrowhead. The markdown keeps every label in reading order: Entrance, the Set box, 'Condition-1 True Exit', False, Execute, Augment. It has no arrows and nothing for the loop-back edge. The order of the labels implies the straight-line flow, but nothing in the text recovers the edge from Augment back to Condition-1, which is what makes this an iteration. The claim quotes both sources correctly. The figure sits in informative Annex D ('not intended to dictate implementation'), so it is not normative, and structural severity fits.
